## What's new: a faster Review, a leaner brief for agents, and many fixes

### Review

- **Accept means Done.** Accept moves the task to Done and nothing else. Accepted work can be reopened from Reviewed with a comment, and the next agent sees that comment first.
- **Review a batch together.** Work that one agent note covered together sits under one heading. Open it to see every task of the batch on one page and accept them in one go. Tasks with something not done, or with unticked criteria, start unticked and say why. "Open on its own" lets you send one task back.
- **Faster to work through.** Shorter rows. A accepts and opens the next task, S starts a comment, J and K move through the list. Accept shows an Undo button for 10 minutes. The single-letter keys can be turned off in Settings > Accessibility, for example for speech input; the buttons and arrow keys keep working.
- **Easier to read.** The report is split into Done, Not done and "For you to check", with the acceptance criteria. When an agent left no report, Moah drafts one from its notes. Drafts now read notes that cover several tasks properly, and they say so when the notes don't mention what is left, instead of claiming nothing is.
- **Work that waits for you reaches Review.** When an agent stops to ask for your OK on a plan, a mockup or a commit, the question waits in Review and the task moves to Blocked. "Approve and continue" answers it without words, and your reply in the agent's chat settles it too.
- **Questions after Done aren't lost.** A question on a task you already accepted or archived starts one "Follow-up to ..." task.
- **Folded groups stay folded,** also after a restart. The screen no longer scrolls on into empty space, and notices no longer cover its buttons.

### Agents

- **A smaller start-up brief.** Project rules are listed by title, and context packs bring a rule's full text when the work needs it. Global rules stay in full. The brief is about a quarter smaller.
- **A smaller tool list.** Tool descriptions are about a fifth shorter, and arguments with a fixed set of values list them, so agents pick a valid one the first time.
- **Notes land on the right task.** When you move the work on in the chat ("Now do CAMP-12"), the agent's notes follow. A checkpoint goes to another task only when its title, or the start of its summary, names that task. A new task can start as in progress.
- **Archive when you ask.** Two new tools, `brain_archive_tasks` and `brain_archive_memories`, let an agent archive or restore tasks and records when you ask it to. Moah keeps your words in the record's history, and locked records are skipped. Nothing is ever deleted.
- **Answers in the chat close questions,** also in the Linux Flatpak and when Claude Code runs in a container such as distrobox.
- **Fewer failed calls.** `brain_list_tasks` takes a single status as text. `brain_update_task` can add only links. "X blocked by Y" marks X as waiting and refuses loops. A new task with almost the same title as an open one gets a warning. `brain_shelves` lists the shelf tree in order. A search for several words also finds records that have all of them but one, after the full matches. In the Claude desktop app, a chat keeps working in the project its brief matched.

### Rules you can rely on

- **Critical rules lock themselves.** A rule marked critical is locked from that moment, whoever marks it, and only you can unlock it. Rules that were critical before this version keep their lock setting: lock them once yourself in Memory.

### Updates and the desktop app

- **Restart after an update.** When a newer version is installed while Moah is open, one line offers Restart now.
- **Agent connections keep up with updates.** When Moah starts, it updates the Claude Code and Codex connections you made with Connect, so an update never asks you to connect again. The Linux Flatpak can't change agent settings from its sandbox, so there Moah tells Claude Code the one command that refreshes an older connection, and the agent asks you before it runs it.
- **The tray menu opens Review** and shows how much waits there. The first time X hides the window, one note says Moah is still running in the tray.
- **Your choices stay.** Theme, language, folded sections, panel widths and the task view are kept after a restart, even when Moah starts on another port.

### Look and feel

- Dropdowns, checkboxes and focus rings look the same everywhere, in both themes.
- **A softer dark theme:** charcoal backgrounds, off-white text and calmer colours, with at least 4.5:1 contrast. The light theme is unchanged.
- Activity is one compact list grouped by day. Your own actions say "You", and a burst of automatic shelf filing shows as one row.
- Search results show each memory type and task status the way the Memory page and the board do, and snippets no longer end in a list of tags.
- Projects without a colour get their own, Brain View fits the window, and AI context says when it picked the task automatically.
- Russian: board headers, Home tiles and labels are no longer cut off, and link types and Brain View details are translated.

### Dictation

- **Microphone settings.** Settings > Dictation holds the dictation language, which microphone to use, and noise reduction, echo removal and automatic volume. A Test button shows whether sound comes in. Nothing is recorded or sent anywhere.
- **No more hanging** on "Finishing the text...". Engine problems go to the error log and show in Diagnostics.

### Focus timer and sounds

- **Sounds have their own card in Settings** and play whether the focus timer is on or off.
- **The desktop timer stays on screen** while the focus timer runs, can be dragged anywhere and remembers its place, and its ring pauses and resumes the timer.

### Fixes

- Diagnostics no longer hangs on Windows, and works in the Linux Flatpak.
- An agent's first answer after an update no longer fails when it is an empty list.
- When Moah updates an agent's settings file, the file keeps its permissions.

### After updating

Quit Moah from the tray and open it again. New agent sessions get the new tools right away; sessions that were already running hear from Moah that they need a restart.
